B.why: Terraced basalt-strata pauldrons with red seams between layers: one strong rock idea that reads from above and is unlike any reference family.
B.fix: Step the terraces harder (each tier narrower, top tier tilted) and thicken the chest crack so it joins the pauldron seams.

C.why: Asymmetric jagged crag on one shoulder is a true mountain silhouette; rest of the body is plain black boxes with thin seams.
C.fix: Grow the crag to break the head line, darken it to basalt with red seams, tie the other pauldron in with a stepped edge.

D.why: Clean, well fitted, best red-seam read (red undersides of sloped pauldrons), but smooth regular slabs read as iron knight in black.
D.fix: Give the pauldrons a rock idea (offset stacked or chipped slabs) and lengthen tassets over the big green hip panel.

A.why: Slanted hood and a small shoulder crag, but light grey trim bands read as iron and parts go to face cross and medallion unseen from above.
A.fix: Turn grey bands to red seams or iron grey, grow the crag into the one silhouette idea.

F.why: Massive cube pauldrons with red outline on every edge: golem bulk but reads as sci-fi trim, not magma seams.
F.fix: Move red into gaps between plates only and break the cube pauldrons into rock slabs.

E.why: Near pure black reads as a blob from above; horn spikes on helm and pauldrons borrow the Reaver language.
E.fix: Lift plates to charcoal, widen seams, replace horns with a basalt crest or column.

notes: All six share the green hip gap (no fauld or short fauld) and all fit the slim avatar without floating parts. B and C carry an actual rock idea; a merge worth trying is B's terraced strata on one shoulder with C's crag rising out of them. Judged from sheets only; no individual close renders were present beyond the sheet panels.
